text:
maria: FYI found a nasty pattern during the canary: encrypted safetensors + bursty prefetch -> KMS QPS spike. nodes prefetching ~60 tiny shards at once triggered lots of KMS:Decrypt throttles this morning.

ajay: Ugh. Is the code doing one KMS call per shard unwrap?

maria: Yup. Each shard header contains a wrapped DEK and we call KMS per header in PrefetchWorker.openShard. Works but scales poorly for many tiny shards.

lily: Short-term: can we add a local rate limiter or staggered prefetch to smooth bursts?

maria: We put a soft limiter but it just moves the tail out. Need a protocol-level fix. Two directions: (A) per-bundle session key (single KMS call -> derive per-shard DEKs via HKDF), or (B) local DEK cache with LRU+TTL.
zane: (A) reduces KMS QPS dramatically. But operationally, some customers with HSM policies won't allow session keys to be persisted even transiently.
samir: Hybrid idea: support session_key path when manifest advertises it, fallback to per-shard unwrap otherwise. Also allow session keys only when control plane asserts bundle policy.
maria: Proposed manifest extension: an optional encryption.session object with {"scheme":"kms-session-v1","derive":"hkdf-sha256","ttl_s":"600"}. Loader attempts session unwrap first. If it succeeds, derive all per-shard DEKs locally. If it fails or session not present, fall back to per-shard unwraps.

kevin: Compliance note: Large customers request audit logs for every KMS unwrap. Session approach changes log semantics (one call for many shards). Product/compliance needs to decide acceptable logging granularity. Control plane should set session_allowed per-customer.
lily: will take that to compliance. For Private clusters default to session_allowed=false unless explicit opt-in.
ajay: Implementation concerns: 1) thundering herd when session unwrap itself hits KMS throttle; 2) memory growth if we cache many derived DEKs.
maria: For (1) plan PrefetchCoordinator per-node with per-bundle in-flight lock. First prefetcher does session unwrap; others wait on result (with bounded timeout/jitter). For (2) cache derived per-shard DEKs keyed by shard-id + bundle-id with eviction and max_items cap. TTL bounded by session TTL.
zane: Also consider cryptographic details: use HKDF with bundle session key -> per-shard DEK. Add salt = shard path and info = bundle-version so rotation works. And zeroize derived keys on eviction.
samir: What about streaming decrypt directly into GPU memory to avoid host copies? Might speed hotstarts but complicates integrity handling and eviction.
maria: Streaming-to-GPU has big edge cases: if integrity check fails mid-stream we need to roll back GPU memory and handle partial writes. Makes cache eviction painful. Not for the first iteration.

kevin: Another op detail: allowlist/session_allowed should be set by registry at bundle publish time. If a bundle moves from private->hosted we may need to flip behavior. Registry must store session_policy and session_allowed bool.
lily: agreed. product will require attestation docs before enabling session_allowed for enterprise customers.
ajay: Metrics to add: kms.session_unwrap_attempts, kms.session_unwrap_success, prefetch.session_wait_ms, prefetch.derived_dek_cache_hit, prefetch.per_shard_unwrap_count. Add a debug trace in PrefetchCoordinator to capture which path was used.
zane: Example manifest snippet (proposal):

```json
{"manifest_v":2,
 "bundle_id":"rwd/llama-13b/v3",
 "encryption":{
   "per_shard_wrap":"wrapped_dek_v1",
   "session":{
     "allowed":true,
     "scheme":"kms-session-v1",
     "derive":"hkdf-sha256",
     "ttl_seconds":600
   }
 },
 "shards":[{"path":"layers/attn.safetensors","size":1234567,"warmup_priority":10},
           {"path":"tokembeds.safetensors","size":9876543,"warmup_priority":50}]
}
```

maria: Loader prefetch sorting change: prefer shards when session_available is true, then by warmup_priority (lower first), then by size ascending. That helps session unwrap benefit small hot prefixes.
samir: Add shard-level hint warmup_priority so model packagers can tune. Also consider an 'enc_priority' for shards that must be available before generating responses.

kevin: For HSM customers we must support a STRICT policy that disallows session path entirely. Enforce at control plane and in the manifest registry. Also support a FALLBACK policy enum: ENFORCED, PERMISSIVE, ALLOW_UNENCRYPTED.
lily: product/compliance: PERMISSIVE for hosted beta, ENFORCED for regulated enterprise until attestation is ready.
ajay: Fallback semantics if both session and per-shard unwrap fail: policy determines behavior: ENFORCED -> fail fast; PERMISSIVE -> try an unencrypted small fallback model if registered; ALLOW_UNENCRYPTED -> auto-fallback. Make these explicit in loader errors and logs.
zane: Test plan: create synthetic canary that issues 300 concurrent warmup requests, measure KMS QPS and error rate, prefetch latency p50/p95, CPU for AES decryption, memory usage of derived key cache, and registry interaction for session_allowed toggles.
maria: I'll write a short RFC patch for manifest v2: encryption.session schema, shards[*].warmup_priority, loader PrefetchCoordinator pseudocode, derived-dek cache semantics, metrics, and rollout plan.

ops-bot: rollout scheduled: canary prefetchnodes pool at 2024-11-03T09:00:00Z (dry-run).

lily: thanks. ping me on the RFC when it's ready so I can send to compliance/product.
maria: will post link here when draft lands. Thanks everyone!
